results.question: Sự khác nhau giữa vun đống lên và vun đống xuống là gì?

message.content:
Sự khác nhau giữa vun đống lên (reheapUp) và vun đống xuống (reheapDown) là:
- Vun đống lên (reheapUp): Sửa một heap bị hỏng bằng cách đẩy phần tử cuối cùng (hoặc phần tử ở vị trí cần xét) lên trên cây cho đến khi nó nằm ở đúng vị trí trong heap.
- Vun đống xuống (reheapDown): Sửa một heap bị hỏng bằng cách đẩy gốc (hoặc phần tử ở vị trí cần xét) xuống dưới cây cho đến khi nó nằm ở đúng vị trí trong heap.

Heap structure.22
Build a Heap
• Given a filled array of elements in random order, to
build the heap we need to rearrange the data so that
each node in the heap is greater than its children.
• We begin by dividing the array into two parts, the left
being a heap and the right being data to be inserted
into the heap. Note the "wall" between the first and
second parts.
• At the beginning the root (the first node) is the only
node in the heap and the rest of the array are data to
be inserted.
• Each iteration of the insertion algorithm uses reheap
up to insert the next element into the heap and moves
the wall separating the elements one position to the
right.

properties:

2 The key value of each node is less than or equal to
the key value in each of its descendents.

The heap is an excellent structure to use for a priority
queue.

high (3), medium (2), and low (1).

fifth are high-priority customers, the third is medium
priority, and the first and the fourth are low priority.

Heap structure.36
Selection Algorithms
Problem
Determining the k^th element in an unsorted list.
Two solutions:
1 Sort the list and select the element at location k. The
complexity of a simple sorting algorithm is O(n^2).
2 Create a heap and delete k −1 elements from the
heap, leaving the desired element at the top. The
complexity is O(n log_2 n).
Rather than simply discarding the elements at the top of
the heap, a better solution would be to place the deleted
element at the end of the heap and reduce the heap size
by 1.
After the k^th element has been processed, the temporarily
removed elements can then be inserted into the heap.

following properties:

Heap structure.16
Heap Data Structure
The relationship between a node and its children is fixed
and can be calculated:
1 For a node located at index i, its children are found at
• Left child: 2i + 1
• Right child: 2i + 2
2 The parent of a node located at index i is located at
⌊(i −1)/2⌋.
3 Given the index for a left child, j, its right sibling, if
any, is found at j + 1. Conversely, given the index for
a right child, k, its left sibling, which must exist, is
found at k −1.
4 Given the size, N, of a complete heap, the location of
the first leaf is ⌊N/2⌋.
5 Given the location of the first leaf element, the
location of the last nonleaf element is 1 less.

last heap node to the root and reheap down.

1 Algorithm HeapSort()
2 Sorts the contiguous list using heap sort.
3 position = count/2 - 1
4 while position >= 0 do
5 ReheapDown(position, count - 1)
6 position = position - 1
7 end
8 last = count - 1
9 while last > 0 do
10 swap(0, last)
11 last = last - 1
12 ReheapDown(0, last - 1)
13 end
14 End HeapSort

Heap structure.22
Build a Heap
• Given a filled array of elements in random order, to
build the heap we need to rearrange the data so that
each node in the heap is greater than its children.
• We begin by dividing the array into two parts, the left
being a heap and the right being data to be inserted
into the heap. Note the "wall" between the first and
second parts.
• At the beginning the root (the first node) is the only
node in the heap and the rest of the array are data to
be inserted.
• Each iteration of the insertion algorithm uses reheap
up to insert the next element into the heap and moves
the wall separating the elements one position to the
right.

Priority Queues
The heap is an excellent structure to use for a priority
queue.
Example
Assume that we have a priority queue with three priorities:
high (3), medium (2), and low (1).
Of the first five customers who arrive, the second and the
fifth are high-priority customers, the third is medium
priority, and the first and the fourth are low priority.

Heap structure.36
Selection Algorithms
Problem
Determining the k^th element in an unsorted list.
Two solutions:
1 Sort the list and select the element at location k. The
complexity of a simple sorting algorithm is O(n^2).
2 Create a heap and delete k −1 elements from the
heap, leaving the desired element at the top. The
complexity is O(n log_2 n).
Rather than simply discarding the elements at the top of
the heap, a better solution would be to place the deleted
element at the end of the heap and reduce the heap size
by 1.
After the k^th element has been processed, the temporarily
removed elements can then be inserted into the heap.

Properties of Heaps
• A complete or nearly complete binary tree.
• If the height is h, the number of nodes N is
between 2^h^−^1 and 2^h −1.
• Complete tree: N = 2^h −1 when last level is full.
• Nearly complete: All nodes in the last level are on
the left.
→Heap can be represented in an array.

A heap (max-heap) is a binary tree structure with the
following properties:

2 The key value of each node is greater than or equal to
the key value in each of its descendents.

Heap Data Structure
The relationship between a node and its children is fixed
and can be calculated:
1 For a node located at index i, its children are found at
• Left child: 2i + 1
• Right child: 2i + 2
2 The parent of a node located at index i is located at
⌊(i −1)/2⌋.
3 Given the index for a left child, j, its right sibling, if
any, is found at j + 1. Conversely, given the index for
a right child, k, its left sibling, which must exist, is
found at k −1.
4 Given the size, N, of a complete heap, the location of
the first leaf is ⌊N/2⌋.
5 Given the location of the first leaf element, the
location of the last nonleaf element is 1 less.

Heap structure.22
Build a Heap
• Given a filled array of elements in random order, to
build the heap we need to rearrange the data so that
each node in the heap is greater than its children.
• We begin by dividing the array into two parts, the left
being a heap and the right being data to be inserted
into the heap. Note the "wall" between the first and
second parts.
• At the beginning the root (the first node) is the only
node in the heap and the rest of the array are data to
be inserted.
• Each iteration of the insertion algorithm uses reheap
up to insert the next element into the heap and moves
the wall separating the elements one position to the
right.

The heap is an excellent structure to use for a priority
queue.
Example
Assume that we have a priority queue with three priorities:
high (3), medium (2), and low (1).
Of the first five customers who arrive, the second and the
fifth are high-priority customers, the third is medium
priority, and the first and the fourth are low priority.

Heap structure.36
Selection Algorithms
Problem
Determining the k^th element in an unsorted list.
Two solutions:
1 Sort the list and select the element at location k. The
complexity of a simple sorting algorithm is O(n^2).
2 Create a heap and delete k −1 elements from the
heap, leaving the desired element at the top. The
complexity is O(n log_2 n).
Rather than simply discarding the elements at the top of
the heap, a better solution would be to place the deleted
element at the end of the heap and reduce the heap size
by 1.
After the k^th element has been processed, the temporarily
removed elements can then be inserted into the heap.

Heap structure.16
Heap Data Structure
The relationship between a node and its children is fixed
and can be calculated:
1 For a node located at index i, its children are found at
• Left child: 2i + 1
• Right child: 2i + 2
2 The parent of a node located at index i is located at
⌊(i −1)/2⌋.
3 Given the index for a left child, j, its right sibling, if
any, is found at j + 1. Conversely, given the index for
a right child, k, its left sibling, which must exist, is
found at k −1.
4 Given the size, N, of a complete heap, the location of
the first leaf is ⌊N/2⌋.
5 Given the location of the first leaf element, the
location of the last nonleaf element is 1 less.

answer.answer:
Sự khác nhau giữa vun đống lên (reheapUp) và vun đống xuống (reheapDown) là:
- Vun đống lên (reheapUp): Sửa một heap bị hỏng bằng cách đẩy phần tử cuối cùng (hoặc phần tử ở vị trí cần xét) lên trên cây cho đến khi nó nằm ở đúng vị trí trong heap.
- Vun đống xuống (reheapDown): Sửa một heap bị hỏng bằng cách đẩy gốc (hoặc phần tử ở vị trí cần xét) xuống dưới cây cho đến khi nó nằm ở đúng vị trí trong heap.

Heap structure.22
Build a Heap
• Given a filled array of elements in random order, to
build the heap we need to rearrange the data so that
each node in the heap is greater than its children.
• We begin by dividing the array into two parts, the left
being a heap and the right being data to be inserted
into the heap. Note the "wall" between the first and
second parts.
• At the beginning the root (the first node) is the only
node in the heap and the rest of the array are data to
be inserted.
• Each iteration of the insertion algorithm uses reheap
up to insert the next element into the heap and moves
the wall separating the elements one position to the
right.

Heap structure.36
Selection Algorithms
Problem
Determining the k^th element in an unsorted list.
Two solutions:
1 Sort the list and select the element at location k. The
complexity of a simple sorting algorithm is O(n^2).
2 Create a heap and delete k −1 elements from the
heap, leaving the desired element at the top. The
complexity is O(n log_2 n).
Rather than simply discarding the elements at the top of
the heap, a better solution would be to place the deleted
element at the end of the heap and reduce the heap size
by 1.
After the k^th element has been processed, the temporarily
removed elements can then be inserted into the heap.

Priority Queues
The heap is an excellent structure to use for a priority
queue.
Example
Assume that we have a priority queue with three priorities:
high (3), medium (2), and low (1).
Of the first five customers who arrive, the second and the
fifth are high-priority customers, the third is medium
priority, and the first and the fourth are low priority.

Heap structure.16
Heap Data Structure
The relationship between a node and its children is fixed
and can be calculated:
1 For a node located at index i, its children are found at
• Left child: 2i + 1
• Right child: 2i + 2
2 The parent of a node located at index i is located at
⌊(i −1)/2⌋.
3 Given the index for a left child, j, its right sibling, if
any, is found at j + 1. Conversely, given the index for
a right child, k, its left sibling, which must exist, is
found at k −1.

• When deleting a node from a heap, the most

last heap node to the root and reheap down.

Selection Algorithms
Problem
Determining the k^th element in an unsorted list.
Two solutions:
1 Sort the list and select the element at location k. The
complexity of a simple sorting algorithm is O(n^2).
2 Create a heap and delete k −1 elements from the
heap, leaving the desired element at the top. The
complexity is O(n log_2 n).
Rather than simply discarding the elements at the top of
the heap, a better solution would be to place the deleted
element at the end of the heap and reduce the heap size
by 1.
After the k^th element has been processed, the temporarily
removed elements can then be inserted into the heap.

Heap Data Structure
The relationship between a node and its children is fixed
and can be calculated:
1 For a node located at index i, its children are found at
• Left child: 2i + 1
• Right child: 2i + 2
2 The parent of a node located at index i is located at
⌊(i −1)/2⌋.
3 Given the index for a left child, j, its right sibling, if
any, is found at j + 1. Conversely, given the index for
a right child, k, its left sibling, which must exist, is
found at k −1.
4 Given the size, N, of a complete heap, the location of
the first leaf is ⌊N/2⌋.
5 Given the location of the first leaf element, the
location of the last nonleaf element is 1 less.

Heap structure.22
Build a Heap
• Given a filled array of elements in random order, to
build the heap we need to rearrange the data so that
each node in the heap is greater than its children.
• We begin by dividing the array into two parts, the left
being a heap and the right being data to be inserted
into the heap. Note the "wall" between the first and
second parts.
• At the beginning the root (the first node) is the only
node in the heap and the rest of the array are data to
be inserted.
• Each iteration of the insertion algorithm uses reheap
up to insert the next element into the heap and moves
the wall separating the elements one position to the
right.

2 Sorts the contiguous list using heap sort.
3 position = count/2 - 1

5 ReheapDown(position, count - 1)

7 end
8 last = count - 1
9 while last > 0 do
10 swap(0, last)
11 last = last - 1
12 ReheapDown(0, last - 1)
13 end
14 End HeapSort

Heap structure.29
Delete a Node from a Heap
• When deleting a node from a heap, the most
common and meaningful logic is to delete the root.
• After it has been deleted, the heap is thus left
without a root.
• To reestablish the heap, we move the data in the
last heap node to the root and reheap down.

Insert a Node into a Heap
• To insert a node, we need to locate the first empty
leaf in the array.
• We find it immediately after the last node in the
tree, which is given as a parameter.
• To insert a node, we move the new data to the
first empty leaf and reheap up.

Heap structure.22
Build a Heap
• Given a filled array of elements in random order, to
build the heap we need to rearrange the data so that
each node in the heap is greater than its children.
• We begin by dividing the array into two parts, the left
being a heap and the right being data to be inserted
into the heap. Note the "wall" between the first and
second parts.
• At the beginning the root (the first node) is the only
node in the heap and the rest of the array are data to
be inserted.
• Each iteration of the insertion algorithm uses reheap
up to insert the next element into the heap and moves
the wall separating the elements one position to the
right.

Heap Definition
Definition
A heap (max-heap) is a binary tree structure with the
following properties:
1 The tree is complete or nearly complete.
2 The key value of each node is greater than or equal to
the key value in each of its descendents.
(Source: Data Structures - A Pseudocode Approach with C++)

Selection Algorithms
Problem
Determining the k^th element in an unsorted list.
Two solutions:
1 Sort the list and select the element at location k. The
complexity of a simple sorting algorithm is O(n^2).
2 Create a heap and delete k −1 elements from the
heap, leaving the desired element at the top. The
complexity is O(n log_2 n).
Rather than simply discarding the elements at the top of
the heap, a better solution would be to place the deleted
element at the end of the heap and reduce the heap size
by 1.
After the k^th element has been processed, the temporarily
removed elements can then be inserted into the heap.

Heap structure.16
Heap Data Structure
The relationship between a node and its children is fixed
and can be calculated:
1 For a node located at index i, its children are found at
• Left child: 2i + 1
• Right child: 2i + 2
2 The parent of a node located at index i is located at
⌊(i −1)/2⌋.
3 Given the index for a left child, j, its right sibling, if
any, is found at j + 1. Conversely, given the index for
a right child, k, its left sibling, which must exist, is
found at k −1.
4 Given the size, N, of a complete heap, the location of
the first leaf is ⌊N/2⌋.
5 Given the location of the first leaf element, the
location of the last nonleaf element is 1 less.

Heap structure.22
Build a Heap
• Given a filled array of elements in random order, to
build the heap we need to rearrange the data so that
each node in the heap is greater than its children.
• We begin by dividing the array into two parts, the left
being a heap and the right being data to be inserted
into the heap. Note the "wall" between the first and
second parts.
• At the beginning the root (the first node) is the only
node in the heap and the rest of the array are data to
be inserted.
• Each iteration of the insertion algorithm uses reheap
up to insert the next element into the heap and moves
the wall separating the elements one position to the
right.

Selection Algorithms
Problem
Determining the k^th element in an unsorted list.
Two solutions:
1 Sort the list and select the element at location k. The
complexity of a simple sorting algorithm is O(n^2).
2 Create a heap and delete k −1 elements from the
heap, leaving the desired element at the top. The
complexity is O(n log_2 n).
Rather than simply discarding the elements at the top of
the heap, a better solution would be to place the deleted
element at the end of the heap and reduce the heap size
by 1.
After the k^th element has been processed, the temporarily
removed elements can then be inserted into the heap.

Heap Data Structure
The relationship between a node and its children is fixed
and can be calculated:
1 For a node located at index i, its children are found at
• Left child: 2i + 1
• Right child: 2i + 2
2 The parent of a node located at index i is located at
⌊(i −1)/2⌋.
3 Given the index for a left child, j, its right sibling, if
any, is found at j + 1. Conversely, given the index for
a right child, k, its left sibling, which must exist, is
found at k −1.
4 Given the size, N, of a complete heap, the location of
the first leaf is ⌊N/2⌋.
5 Given the location of the first leaf element, the
location of the last nonleaf element is 1 less.

queue.

fifth are high-priority customers, the third is medium
priority, and the first and the fourth are low priority.

• When deleting a node from a heap, the most
common and meaningful logic is to delete the root.
• After it has been deleted, the heap is thus left
without a root.
• To reestablish the heap, we move the data in the
last heap node to the root and reheap down.

Priority Queues
The heap is an excellent structure to use for a priority
queue.
Example
Assume that we have a priority queue with three priorities:
high (3), medium (2), and low (1).
Of the first five customers who arrive, the second and the
fifth are high-priority customers, the third is medium
priority, and the first and the fourth are low priority.
(Source: Data Structures - A Pseudocode Approach with C++)

Heap structure.36
Selection Algorithms
Problem
Determining the k^th element in an unsorted list.
Two solutions:
1 Sort the list and select the element at location k. The
complexity of a simple sorting algorithm is O(n^2).
2 Create a heap and delete k −1 elements from the
heap, leaving the desired element at the top. The
complexity is O(n log_2 n).
Rather than simply discarding the elements at the top of
the heap, a better solution would be to place the deleted
element at the end of the heap and reduce the heap size
by 1.
After the k^th element has been processed, the temporarily
removed elements can then be inserted into the heap.

Heap structure.22
Build a Heap
• Given a filled array of elements in random order, to
build the heap we need to rearrange the data so that
each node in the heap is greater than its children.
• We begin by dividing the array into two parts, the left
being a heap and the right being data to be inserted
into the heap. Note the "wall" between the first and
second parts.
• At the beginning the root (the first node) is the only
node in the heap and the rest of the array are data to
be inserted.
• Each iteration of the insertion algorithm uses reheap
up to insert the next element into the heap and moves
the wall separating the elements one position to the
right.

Heap structure.16
Heap Data Structure
The relationship between a node and its children is fixed
and can be calculated:
1 For a node located at index i, its children are found at
• Left child: 2i + 1
• Right child: 2i + 2
2 The parent of a node located at index i is located at
⌊(i −1)/2⌋.
3 Given the index for a left child, j, its right sibling, if
any, is found at j + 1. Conversely, given the index for
a right child, k, its left sibling, which must exist, is
found at k −1.
4 Given the size, N, of a complete heap, the location of
the first leaf is ⌊N/2⌋.
5 Given the location of the first leaf element, the
location of the last nonleaf element is 1 less.

Selection Algorithms
Problem
Determining the k^th element in an unsorted list.
Two solutions:
1 Sort the list and select the element at location k. The
complexity of a simple sorting algorithm is O(n^2).
2 Create a heap and delete k −1 elements from the
heap, leaving the desired element at the top. The
complexity is O(n log_2 n).
Rather than simply discarding the elements at the top of
the heap, a better solution would be to place the deleted
element at the end of the heap and reduce the heap size
by 1.
After the k^th element has been processed, the temporarily
removed elements can then be inserted into the heap.

Heap structure.22
Build a Heap
• Given a filled array of elements in random order, to
build the heap we need to rearrange the data so that
each node in the heap is greater than its children.
• We begin by dividing the array into two parts, the left
being a heap and the right being data to be inserted
into the heap. Note the "wall" between the first and
second parts.
• At the beginning the root (the first node) is the only
node in the heap and the rest of the array are data to
be inserted.
• Each iteration of the insertion algorithm uses reheap
up to insert the next element into the heap and moves
the wall separating the elements one position to the
right.

Heap Data Structure
The relationship between a node and its children is fixed
and can be calculated:
1 For a node located at index i, its children are found at
• Left child: 2i + 1
• Right child: 2i + 2
2 The parent of a node located at index i is located at
⌊(i −1)/2⌋.
3 Given the index for a left child, j, its right sibling, if
any, is found at j + 1. Conversely, given the index for
a right child, k, its left sibling, which must exist, is
found at k −1.
4 Given the size, N, of a complete heap, the location of
the first leaf is ⌊N/2⌋.
5 Given the location of the first leaf element, the
location of the last nonleaf element is 1 less.

Heap structure.36
Selection Algorithms
Problem
Determining the k^th element in an unsorted list.
Two solutions:
1 Sort the list and select the element at location k. The
complexity of a simple sorting algorithm is O(n^2).
2 Create a heap and delete k −1 elements from the
heap, leaving the desired element at the top. The
complexity is O(n log_2 n).
Rather than simply discarding the elements at the top of
the heap, a better solution would be to place the deleted
element at the end of the heap and reduce the heap size
by 1.
After the k^th element has been processed, the temporarily
removed elements can then be inserted into the heap.

Heap Data Structure
The relationship between a node and its children is fixed
and can be calculated:
1 For a node located at index i, its children are found at
• Left child: 2i + 1
• Right child: 2i + 2
2 The parent of a node located at index i is located at
⌊(i −1)/2⌋.
3 Given the index for a left child, j, its right sibling, if
any, is found at j + 1. Conversely, given the index for
a right child, k, its left sibling, which must exist, is
found at k −1.
4 Given the size, N, of a complete heap, the location of
the first leaf is ⌊N/2⌋.
5 Given the location of the first leaf element, the
location of the last nonleaf element is 1 less.

Heap structure.22
Build a Heap
• Given a filled array of elements in random order, to
build the heap we need to rearrange the data so that
each node in the heap is greater than its children.
• We begin by dividing the array into two parts, the left
being a heap and the right being data to be inserted
into the heap. Note the "wall" between the first and
second parts.
• At the beginning the root (the first node) is the only
node in the heap and the rest of the array are data to
be inserted.
• Each iteration of the insertion algorithm uses reheap
up to insert the next element into the heap and moves
the wall separating the elements one position to the
right.

Delete a Node from a Heap
• When deleting a node from a heap, the most
common and meaningful logic is to delete the root.
• After it has been deleted, the heap is thus left
without a root.

Heap structure.36
Selection Algorithms
Problem
Determining the k^th element in an unsorted list.
Two solutions:
1 Sort the list and select the element at location k. The
complexity of a simple sorting algorithm is O(n^2).
2 Create a heap and delete k −1 elements from the
heap, leaving the desired element at the top. The
complexity is O(n log_2 n).
Rather than simply discarding the elements at the top of
the heap, a better solution would be to place the deleted
element at the end of the heap and reduce the heap size
by 1.
After the k^th element has been processed, the temporarily
removed elements can then be inserted into the heap.

Heap Data Structure
The relationship between a node and its children is fixed
and can be calculated:
1 For a node located at index i, its children are found at
• Left child: 2i + 1
• Right child: 2i + 2
2 The parent of a node located at index i is located at
⌊(i −1)/2⌋.
3 Given the index for a left child, j, its right sibling, if
any, is found at j + 1. Conversely, given the index for
a right child, k, its left sibling, which must exist, is
found at k −1.
4 Given the size, N, of a complete heap, the location of
the first leaf is ⌊N/2⌋.
5 Given the location of the first leaf element, the
location of the last nonleaf element is 1 less.

Heap Data Structure
The relationship between a node and its children is fixed
and can be calculated:
1 For a node located at index i, its children are found at
• Left child: 2i + 1
• Right child: 2i + 2
2 The parent of a node located at index i is located at
⌊(i −1)/2⌋.
3 Given the index for a left child, j, its right sibling, if
any, is found at j + 1. Conversely, given the index for
a right child, k, its left sibling, which must exist, is
found at k −1.
4 Given the size, N, of a complete heap, the location of
the first leaf is ⌊N/2⌋.
5 Given the location of the first leaf element, the
location of the last nonleaf element is 1 less.

Heap structure.22
Build a Heap
• Given a filled array of elements in random order, to
build the heap we need to rearrange the data so that
each node in the heap is greater than its children.
• We begin by dividing the array into two parts, the left
being a heap and the right being data to be inserted
into the heap. Note the "wall" between the first and
second parts.
• At the beginning the root (the first node) is the only
node in the heap and the rest of the array are data to
be inserted.
• Each iteration of the insertion algorithm uses reheap
up to insert the next element into the heap and moves
the wall separating the elements one position to the
right.

queue.

fifth are high-priority customers, the third is medium
priority, and the first and the fourth are low priority.

Selection Algorithms
Problem
Determining the k^th element in an unsorted list.
Two solutions:
1 Sort the list and select the element at location k. The
complexity of a simple sorting algorithm is O(n^2).
2 Create a heap and delete k −1 elements from the
heap, leaving the desired element at the top. The
complexity is O(n log_2 n).
Rather than simply discarding the elements at the top of
the heap, a better solution would be to place the deleted
element at the end of the heap and reduce the heap size
by 1.
After the k^th element has been processed, the temporarily
removed elements can then be inserted into the heap.

Heap Data Structure
The relationship between a node and its children is fixed
and can be calculated:
1 For a node located at index i, its children are found at
• Left child: 2i + 1
• Right child: 2i + 2
2 The parent of a node located at index i is located at
⌊(i −1)/2⌋.
3 Given the index for a left child, j, its right sibling, if
any, is found at j + 1. Conversely, given the index for
a right child, k, its left sibling, which must exist, is
found at k −1.
4 Given the size, N, of a complete heap, the location of
the first leaf is ⌊N/2⌋.
5 Given the location of the first leaf element, the
location of the last nonleaf element is 1 less.

following properties:

the key value in each of its descendents.

Heap structure.22
Build a Heap
• Given a filled array of elements in random order, to
build the heap we need to rearrange the data so that
each node in the heap is greater than its children.
• We begin by dividing the array into two parts, the left
being a heap and the right being data to be inserted
into the heap. Note the "wall" between the first and
second parts.
• At the beginning the root (the first node) is the only
node in the heap and the rest of the array are data to
be inserted.
• Each iteration of the insertion algorithm uses reheap
up to insert the next element into the heap and moves
the wall separating the elements one position to the
right.

The heap is an excellent structure to use for a priority
queue.
Example
Assume that we have a priority queue with three priorities:
high (3), medium (2), and low (1).
Of the first five customers who arrive, the second and the
fifth are high-priority customers, the third is medium
priority, and the first and the fourth are low priority.

Properties of Heaps
• A complete or nearly complete binary tree.
• If the height is h, the number of nodes N is
between 2^h^−^1 and 2^h −1.
• Complete tree: N = 2^h −1 when last level is full.
• Nearly complete: All nodes in the last level are on
the left.
→Heap can be represented in an array.

13 end

• When deleting a node from a heap, the most
common and meaningful logic is to delete the root.

last heap node to the root and reheap down.

Selection Algorithms
Problem
Determining the k^th element in an unsorted list.
Two solutions:
1 Sort the list and select the element at location k. The
complexity of a simple sorting algorithm is O(n^2).
2 Create a heap and delete k −1 elements from the
heap, leaving the desired element at the top. The
complexity is O(n log_2 n).
Rather than simply discarding the elements at the top of
the heap, a better solution would be to place the deleted
element at the end of the heap and reduce the heap size
by 1.
After the k^th element has been processed, the temporarily
removed elements can then be inserted into the heap.

Heap structure.16
Heap Data Structure
The relationship between a node and its children is fixed
and can be calculated:
1 For a node located at index i, its children are found at
• Left child: 2i + 1
• Right child: 2i + 2
2 The parent of a node located at index i is located at
⌊(i −1)/2⌋.
3 Given the index for a left child, j, its right sibling, if
any, is found at j + 1. Conversely, given the index for
a right child, k, its left sibling, which must exist, is
found at k −1.
4 Given the size, N, of a complete heap, the location of
the first leaf is ⌊N/2⌋.
5 Given the location of the first leaf element, the
location of the last nonleaf element is 1 less.

Heap structure.22
Build a Heap
• Given a filled array of elements in random order, to
build the heap we need to rearrange the data so that
each node in the heap is greater than its children.
• We begin by dividing the array into two parts, the left
being a heap and the right being data to be inserted
into the heap. Note the "wall" between the first and
second parts.
• At the beginning the root (the first node) is the only
node in the heap and the rest of the array are data to
be inserted.
• Each iteration of the insertion algorithm uses reheap
up to insert the next element into the heap and moves
the wall separating the elements one position to the
right.

The heap is an excellent structure to use for a priority
queue.

fifth are high-priority customers, the third is medium
priority, and the first and the fourth are low priority.

Selection Algorithms
Problem
Determining the k^th element in an unsorted list.
Two solutions:
1 Sort the list and select the element at location k. The
complexity of a simple sorting algorithm is O(n^2).
2 Create a heap and delete k −1 elements from the
heap, leaving the desired element at the top. The
complexity is O(n log_2 n).
Rather than simply discarding the elements at the top of
the heap, a better solution would be to place the deleted
element at the end of the heap and reduce the heap size
by 1.
After the k^th element has been processed, the temporarily
removed elements can then be inserted into the heap.

Heap structure.16
Heap Data Structure
The relationship between a node and its children is fixed
and can be calculated:
1 For a node located at index i, its children are found at
• Left child: 2i + 1
• Right child: 2i + 2
2 The parent of a node located at index i is located at
⌊(i −1)/2⌋.
3 Given the index for a left child, j, its right sibling, if
any, is found at j + 1. Conversely, given the index for
a right child, k, its left sibling, which must exist, is
found at k −1.
4 Given the size, N, of a complete heap, the location of
the first leaf is ⌊N/2⌋.
5 Given the location of the first leaf element, the
location of the last nonleaf element is 1 less.

Heap structure.22
Build a Heap
• Given a filled array of elements in random order, to
build the heap we need to rearrange the data so that
each node in the heap is greater than its children.
• We begin by dividing the array into two parts, the left
being a heap and the right being data to be inserted
into the heap. Note the "wall" between the first and
second parts.
• At the beginning the root (the first node) is the only
node in the heap and the rest of the array are data to
be inserted.
• Each iteration of the insertion algorithm uses reheap
up to insert the next element into the heap and moves
the wall separating the elements one position to the
right.

message.content: The reheapUp operation repairs a "broken" heap by floating the last element up the tree until it is in its correct location in the heap (reestablishes the heap by moving data in position up to its correct location). On the other hand, the reheapDown operation repairs a "broken" heap by pushing the root down the tree until it is in its correct location in the heap (reestablishes the heap by moving data in position down to its correct location).

Heap structure.22
Build a Heap
• Given a filled array of elements in random order, to
build the heap we need to rearrange the data so that
each node in the heap is greater than its children.
• We begin by dividing the array into two parts, the left
being a heap and the right being data to be inserted
into the heap. Note the "wall" between the first and
second parts.
• At the beginning the root (the first node) is the only
node in the heap and the rest of the array are data to
be inserted.
• Each iteration of the insertion algorithm uses reheap
up to insert the next element into the heap and moves
the wall separating the elements one position to the
right.

Heap structure.36
Selection Algorithms
Problem
Determining the k^th element in an unsorted list.
Two solutions:
1 Sort the list and select the element at location k. The
complexity of a simple sorting algorithm is O(n^2).
2 Create a heap and delete k −1 elements from the
heap, leaving the desired element at the top. The
complexity is O(n log_2 n).
Rather than simply discarding the elements at the top of
the heap, a better solution would be to place the deleted
element at the end of the heap and reduce the heap size
by 1.
After the k^th element has been processed, the temporarily
removed elements can then be inserted into the heap.

Heap Data Structure
The relationship between a node and its children is fixed
and can be calculated:
1 For a node located at index i, its children are found at
• Left child: 2i + 1
• Right child: 2i + 2
2 The parent of a node located at index i is located at
⌊(i −1)/2⌋.
3 Given the index for a left child, j, its right sibling, if
any, is found at j + 1. Conversely, given the index for
a right child, k, its left sibling, which must exist, is
found at k −1.
4 Given the size, N, of a complete heap, the location of
the first leaf is ⌊N/2⌋.
5 Given the location of the first leaf element, the
location of the last nonleaf element is 1 less.

Heap structure.22
Build a Heap
• Given a filled array of elements in random order, to
build the heap we need to rearrange the data so that
each node in the heap is greater than its children.
• We begin by dividing the array into two parts, the left
being a heap and the right being data to be inserted
into the heap. Note the "wall" between the first and
second parts.
• At the beginning the root (the first node) is the only
node in the heap and the rest of the array are data to
be inserted.
• Each iteration of the insertion algorithm uses reheap
up to insert the next element into the heap and moves
the wall separating the elements one position to the
right.

Heap Data Structure
The relationship between a node and its children is fixed
and can be calculated:
1 For a node located at index i, its children are found at
• Left child: 2i + 1
• Right child: 2i + 2
2 The parent of a node located at index i is located at
⌊(i −1)/2⌋.
3 Given the index for a left child, j, its right sibling, if
any, is found at j + 1. Conversely, given the index for
a right child, k, its left sibling, which must exist, is
found at k −1.
4 Given the size, N, of a complete heap, the location of
the first leaf is ⌊N/2⌋.
5 Given the location of the first leaf element, the
location of the last nonleaf element is 1 less.

Heap structure.36
Selection Algorithms
Problem
Determining the k^th element in an unsorted list.
Two solutions:
1 Sort the list and select the element at location k. The
complexity of a simple sorting algorithm is O(n^2).
2 Create a heap and delete k −1 elements from the
heap, leaving the desired element at the top. The
complexity is O(n log_2 n).
Rather than simply discarding the elements at the top of
the heap, a better solution would be to place the deleted
element at the end of the heap and reduce the heap size
by 1.
After the k^th element has been processed, the temporarily
removed elements can then be inserted into the heap.

Heap structure.22
Build a Heap
• Given a filled array of elements in random order, to
build the heap we need to rearrange the data so that
each node in the heap is greater than its children.
• We begin by dividing the array into two parts, the left
being a heap and the right being data to be inserted
into the heap. Note the "wall" between the first and
second parts.
• At the beginning the root (the first node) is the only
node in the heap and the rest of the array are data to
be inserted.
• Each iteration of the insertion algorithm uses reheap
up to insert the next element into the heap and moves
the wall separating the elements one position to the
right.

• Nearly complete: All nodes in the last level are on
the left.

Heap structure.16
Heap Data Structure
The relationship between a node and its children is fixed
and can be calculated:
1 For a node located at index i, its children are found at
• Left child: 2i + 1
• Right child: 2i + 2
2 The parent of a node located at index i is located at
⌊(i −1)/2⌋.
3 Given the index for a left child, j, its right sibling, if
any, is found at j + 1. Conversely, given the index for
a right child, k, its left sibling, which must exist, is
found at k −1.
4 Given the size, N, of a complete heap, the location of
the first leaf is ⌊N/2⌋.
5 Given the location of the first leaf element, the
location of the last nonleaf element is 1 less.

Heap structure.36
Selection Algorithms
Problem
Determining the k^th element in an unsorted list.
Two solutions:
1 Sort the list and select the element at location k. The
complexity of a simple sorting algorithm is O(n^2).
2 Create a heap and delete k −1 elements from the
heap, leaving the desired element at the top. The
complexity is O(n log_2 n).
Rather than simply discarding the elements at the top of
the heap, a better solution would be to place the deleted
element at the end of the heap and reduce the heap size
by 1.
After the k^th element has been processed, the temporarily
removed elements can then be inserted into the heap.

Priority Queues
The heap is an excellent structure to use for a priority
queue.
Example
Assume that we have a priority queue with three priorities:
high (3), medium (2), and low (1).
Of the first five customers who arrive, the second and the
fifth are high-priority customers, the third is medium
priority, and the first and the fourth are low priority.

Delete a Node from a Heap
• When deleting a node from a heap, the most
common and meaningful logic is to delete the root.
• After it has been deleted, the heap is thus left
without a root.
• To reestablish the heap, we move the data in the
last heap node to the root and reheap down.

queue.

fifth are high-priority customers, the third is medium
priority, and the first and the fourth are low priority.

Heap structure.22
Build a Heap
• Given a filled array of elements in random order, to
build the heap we need to rearrange the data so that
each node in the heap is greater than its children.
• We begin by dividing the array into two parts, the left
being a heap and the right being data to be inserted
into the heap. Note the "wall" between the first and
second parts.
• At the beginning the root (the first node) is the only
node in the heap and the rest of the array are data to
be inserted.
• Each iteration of the insertion algorithm uses reheap
up to insert the next element into the heap and moves
the wall separating the elements one position to the
right.

• Nearly complete: All nodes in the last level are on
the left.

Heap structure.36
Selection Algorithms
Problem
Determining the k^th element in an unsorted list.
Two solutions:
1 Sort the list and select the element at location k. The
complexity of a simple sorting algorithm is O(n^2).
2 Create a heap and delete k −1 elements from the
heap, leaving the desired element at the top. The
complexity is O(n log_2 n).
Rather than simply discarding the elements at the top of
the heap, a better solution would be to place the deleted
element at the end of the heap and reduce the heap size
by 1.
After the k^th element has been processed, the temporarily
removed elements can then be inserted into the heap.

Heap structure.16
Heap Data Structure
The relationship between a node and its children is fixed
and can be calculated:
1 For a node located at index i, its children are found at
• Left child: 2i + 1
• Right child: 2i + 2
2 The parent of a node located at index i is located at
⌊(i −1)/2⌋.
3 Given the index for a left child, j, its right sibling, if
any, is found at j + 1. Conversely, given the index for
a right child, k, its left sibling, which must exist, is
found at k −1.
4 Given the size, N, of a complete heap, the location of
the first leaf is ⌊N/2⌋.
5 Given the location of the first leaf element, the
location of the last nonleaf element is 1 less.

retrieval_trace.query: What is the difference between reheap up and reheap down?

answer.answer: The reheapUp operation repairs a "broken" heap by floating the last element up the tree until it is in its correct location in the heap (reestablishes the heap by moving data in position up to its correct location). On the other hand, the reheapDown operation repairs a "broken" heap by pushing the root down the tree until it is in its correct location in the heap (reestablishes the heap by moving data in position down to its correct location).

Tìm kiếm nhị phân
Tìm kiếm nhị phân là thuật toán tìm một phần tử trong mảng đã sắp xếp bằng cách liên tục chia đôi khoảng tìm kiếm. Mỗi bước so sánh phần tử ở giữa mảng với giá trị cần tìm: nếu bằng thì trả về vị trí đó; nếu nhỏ hơn thì tìm ở nửa phải; nếu lớn hơn thì tìm ở nửa trái. Độ phức tạp thời gian là O(log n) vì mỗi bước loại bỏ một nửa số phần tử còn lại. Điều kiện bắt buộc: mảng đầu vào phải được sắp xếp trước. Nếu chưa được sắp xếp, thuật toán có thể trả kết quả sai.

Tìm kiếm tuyến tính
Tìm kiếm tuyến tính kiểm tra từng phần tử từ đầu đến cuối mảng, có độ phức tạp thời gian O(n). Thuật toán không yêu cầu mảng được sắp xếp.
